classification.difficultyReason: Connect midpoint half-lengths to one common set of three side lengths for all four triangles, then distinguish SSS congruence from SSS similarity to the original triangle.

content.prompt: Prove that: The intervals joining the midpoints of the sides of a triangle dissect the triangle into four congruent triangles each similar to the original triangle.

spec.description: Four-triangle midpoint subdivision with triple, double and single midpoint tick pairs; ordinary marks black and no shading.
spec.mathematics: AR=RB, AQ=QC, BP=PC; RQ,RP,QP form the central triangle.

answer.short: All four small triangles are congruent (SSS), and each is similar to $\triangle ABC$ with scale factor $\frac12$.
answer.worked:
By the midpoint theorem,
$$\begin{align*}RQ&=\frac12BC=BP=PC\\RP&=\frac12AC=AQ=QC\\QP&=\frac12AB=AR=RB\end{align*}$$
Each of the four triangles has side lengths $\frac12AB$, $\frac12BC$ and $\frac12AC$. Therefore $\triangle ARQ\cong\triangle RBP\cong\triangle QPC\cong\triangle PQR$ (SSS). Each small triangle has its three sides proportional to the corresponding sides of $\triangle ABC$, with ratio $1:2$. Hence each is similar to $\triangle ABC$ (SSS similarity).
